header:
Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Vela), Ben Lowe (ML Eng), Markus Chen (Infra)
summary: Initial discovery for migrating Vela Robotics' LLM workloads from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Discussed compatibility with vLLM/TGI runtimes, eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and proposed pilot and benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samira from Redwood here, happy to kick off. Can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Aisha: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:08] Ben: Hi all.
[00:10] Diego: Hi, Diego Ramos, systems SE at Redwood. I'll be the tech lead on this call.
[00:15] Aisha: Great. So quick context: we're currently using OpenAI for most of our inference, and we are evaluating options to move to either a dedicated hosted setup or a private/VPC on-premish deployment. Main drivers are cost predictability, lower tail latency for real-time robotics control prompts, and data residency.
[00:28] Samira: Perfect, that's exactly what we expected. Can you give a bit more color on volumes, token rates, and any hard latency SLOs?
[00:35] Aisha: Sure. Right now peak is about 600 reqs/min for our perception assistant, avg prompt size ~250 tokens, completions ~150 tokens. Latency SLOs: 95th p95 target is sub-120ms for the decode phase in production. We also do a lot of embeddings for semantic search, batched offline.
[00:50] Ben: To add, we use a mix of chat-style prompts and API calls via openai completions endpoint. Some of our infra folks run vLLM on-prem for internal experiments, and we've tried TGI for a couple of models. There's a bit of fragmentation.
[01:05] Diego: Got it. When you say vLLM experiments, is that full production or just PoC? Any custom kernels or heavy KV cache tweaks?
[01:12] Ben: Mostly PoC. We've tuned kv cache parameters and kept things on A100s for those runs. Not production. Production is OpenAI.
[01:18] Markus: From infra side we care about network egress cost, encrypted-in-transit, KMS for key separation, and SSO. We'd like to see audit logs and per-user RBAC.
[01:27] Samira: Totally reasonable. Redwood Dedicated can be provisioned in a VPC with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) and per-token cost reporting. We also have audit logs and RBAC.
[01:36] Aisha: How close is Redwood's API to OpenAI? We have a lot of code that calls OpenAI endpoints; rewriting is a risk.
[01:44] Diego: Good question. We aim for API parity for the common generation and chat flows. Most customers can switch with a small shim layer. There are edge cases — for example function-calling differences and model names. Also, if you depend on specific OpenAI-only features, we should map them.
[01:58] Ben: And what about model parity? If we migrate, we need the same quality. Our eval suite is pretty strict — we run human-in-the-loop checks and automated evals.
[02:08] Samira: We do controlled eval parity tests. Typically we run your evaluation prompts against our curated model catalog and compare output distributions and metrics. For the pilot we can run side-by-side comparisons against OpenAI and report BLEU/ROUGE and human judgments.
[02:20] Aisha: That would help. Also latency — are you able to meet the 120ms p95?
[02:25] Diego: Depends on model size and hardware. For smaller Llama-2 style models on optimized GPUs and our compilation/kernels, hitting sub-120ms p95 for the decode portion is possible for many configs. For larger models or heavier context you may need tuned batching and warm caches.
[02:40] Markus: We're concerned about cold-starts and KV cache warmup — our robot control path can't tolerate spikes.
[02:46] Diego: We support prefix caching and pre-warm techniques. Also steady-state batching can be limited at the routing layer to keep latency low. We can instrument traces so you see per-token breakdowns.
[02:56] Ben: You mentioned vLLM/TGI. We run some TGI for faster throughput. How compatible are saved checkpoints?
[03:03] Diego: We support most Hugging Face checkpoints and can ingest TGI/vLLM-compatible artifacts, though there can be differences in quantization metadata. In some cases a quick conversion or recompile is necessary. We usually handle that during model onboarding.
[03:16] Aisha: Any known gotchas? We tried migrating a small model and saw behavior shifts on a few prompts.
[03:22] Diego: Behavior shifts can happen due to tokenization differences or subtle kernel optimizations. That's why we do eval parity and recommend running your test-suite during onboarding. Also quantization profiles can affect generation quality.
[03:34] Markus: Security questions — SOC2? ISO?
[03:37] Samira: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant and maintains ISO 27001 controls for Dedicated customers. For Private deployments we support customer-managed control plane and can sign addendums. We'll share the security pack.
[03:48] Aisha: Can we do on-prem/offline? Some of our customers require air-gapped options.
[03:52] Samira: Yes, we have Private deployment options that are fully air-gapped with an on-prem bundle. There are operational tradeoffs and longer lead-times.
[03:59] Ben: Cost — rough order of magnitude. We're paying X to OpenAI; need predictable monthly committed costs.
[04:05] Samira: For Dedicated we provide reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual) and show token-level billing. We'll send you a pricing sheet with examples using your volumes. Committed usage reduces per-token significantly versus hosted.
[04:18] Markus: Networking — can Redwood sit inside our VPC and avoid egress?
[04:22] Diego: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in your cloud account, or we can place nodes in a customer VPC. That avoids public egress and meets residency constraints.
[04:30] Aisha: Great. For pilot scope, we're thinking a subset of the perception assistant — about 10% of traffic routed to Redwood, run side-by-side for 2 weeks. Does that sound reasonable?
[04:39] Samira: Perfect. Typical pilot steps: 1) onboarding + model import, 2) run eval parity tests, 3) perf benchmarks at your traffic profile, 4) short production canary. Diego, you'll be the lead on perf tests?
[04:50] Diego: Yep, I'll run benchmarks and work with Markus to provision VPC/Dedicated nodes. If you can share a representative prompt set and sample logs, we can simulate the workload.
[04:59] Ben: We'll need a simple shim to switch endpoints. How long does onboarding take?
[05:04] Samira: For a small pilot, onboarding can be as short as 3-5 business days once we have models and access. Private or on-prem takes longer.
[05:12] Aisha: About compliance: we need KMS and strict key separation so that no Redwood shared key can decrypt PII. Is that supported?
[05:20] Samira: Yes, customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations are supported on Dedicated/Private. We'll provide the security docs with specifics.
[05:29] Markus: Does Redwood retain logs/token-level data by default? We need to ensure we can opt-out or configure retention.
[05:34] Diego: We have configurable retention policies and can disable retention for certain endpoints. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:41] Ben: One more on model format: we currently store LoRA adapters for some tasks. Can Redwood apply LoRA or adapters at runtime?
[05:49] Diego: We support LoRA-style adapters in some runtimes, though runtime support depends on the exact format. If you can share a sample adapter, we can test during onboarding.
[05:59] Aisha: Okay fair. How about the operational side — tracing, dashboards?
[06:03] Samira: Redwood Console gives per-route latency, token cost, trace sampling, and error breakdowns. We can add tracing hooks for your existing instrumentation.
[06:12] Markus: Any SLA for Dedicated? We need 99.9 uptime and latency SLOs.
[06:16] Samira: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and a set of latency targets you can negotiate. We'll include that in the enterprise agreement.
[06:24] Ben: From a developer perspective, are there SDKs similar to openai-python?
[06:28] Diego: Yes, SDKs in Python, Node, and Go. We mimic popular client patterns, so switching is straightforward.
[06:34] Aisha: On eval parity, will Redwood provide raw outputs so our evaluators can blind-test?
[06:39] Samira: Absolutely. We can export the outputs and run blind evaluations. We'll also provide deterministic seeding where possible for reproducibility.
[06:47] Ben: Can we run a few adversarial prompts to check for regression relative to OpenAI?
[06:52] Diego: Yes, that's standard in our onboarding. We'll run your adversarial test set and generate a report.
[06:58] Aisha: Any technical debt concerns — we have stateful streaming sessions and KV cache behaviors for long-running contexts.
[07:06] Diego: We support KV cache semantics and session affinity; the implementation details differ but we provide a migration guide to map session state. We'll validate with your test-suite.
[07:18] Markus: Are there any uplift costs for moving models from TGI/vLLM to Redwood compiled runtime?
[07:23] Diego: Usually minimal — a short recompile step and validation. For quantized checkpoints you might want to re-quantize with our recommended profiles. We help with that during onboarding.
[07:35] Samira: To summarize, agreed pilot: 2-week side-by-side on perception assistant, we run eval parity and perf benchmarks, Redwood to supply pricing and security pack, Vela to share prompts, logs, and adapters.
[07:48] Aisha: Sounds good. Timing — can we do the technical deep dive next Tuesday?
[07:52] Samira: Next Tue works, I'll send an invite.
[07:55] Ben: Thanks.
[07:56] Markus: One last question — are there examples of other robotics customers?
[08:00] Samira: We have a couple of case studies (anonymized) around low-latency control loops and edge deployments; I'll include links.
[08:08] Aisha: Perfect.
[08:10] Samira: Okay I will send the pricing and security docs this week and Diego will follow up with the benchmark plan. Any other items?
[08:17] Ben: No, that's it.
[08:18] Aisha: Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Diego: Thanks all. We'll send the spreadsheet with the benchmark config and a rough timeline.
[08:26] Samira: Great — we'll reconvene after the tech deep dive.
[08:30] [Call ends]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription noise and minor name mis-hearings. Shared artifacts: security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/vela-pack), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/vela-benchmark.xlsx).
